answer: Bonded staking registries mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock escrowed capital before transacting. Filtering admission through this economic prism imposes a verifiable cost of illiquid capital per identity, rendering cheap automated clones an impossible fable. This mechanism builds a capital canyon that priced-out adversaries cannot easily cross. A core limitation is that strict financial thresholds disadvantage resource-poor honest agents while favoring well-funded entities.
